comments.comment: Unused items: _in_bounds(), as well as imports copy as _copy and itertools as _it are not used. Consider removing to reduce clutter.

check_winner: winning_line is returned as a lexicographically sorted list of coordinates, which may not preserve the geometric order along the line (especially for diagonals). This is fine for your current per-stone highlight, but if later you draw a connecting line, keep the natural end-to-end order by walking from one end to the other.

start_new_game(): consider invalidating any in-flight AI job by incrementing ai_job_id when restarting (even when Human starts). It already works due to the AI-turn check and the new schedule when AI starts, but explicitly bumping the job id on restart makes staleness handling more robust to future changes.
import time is unused. Remove unused import.
compute_best_move() ignores the time_limit argument (the algorithm is fast enough, so it's fine). Optionally document this or enforce a soft cap if future heuristics become more expensive.

set_difficulty_display() and set_starter_display() reset the info label to 'Turn: --'. Because the controller immediately calls set_turn() after difficulty/starter changes, users won’t see this for long, but it can cause a brief flicker. Consider keeping the existing 'Turn: ...' line and only updating the relevant parts to avoid transient inconsistency.

summary: Overall, the implementation adheres well to the specified MVC architecture and satisfies the functional and non-functional requirements for a 15x15 Gomoku with Tkinter UI and AI opponent. Public interfaces match exactly, the app is runnable via main.main(), turn/order enforcement is correct, AI difficulty behaviors meet the minimum acceptance criteria (Medium/Hard block single win-in-one, Hard takes immediate win), and UI provides snapping, last-move marker, winning line highlight, and clear status. AI runs on a background thread with job-id staleness protection, keeping the UI responsive. Only minor issues are noted below; none are blocking.
